[After successfully capturing the Carthaginian city of Cartagena]

When one of the captive women, the wife of Mandonius, who was brother to Andobales, King of the Ilergetes, fell at his feet and entreated him with tears to treat them with more proper consideration than the Carthaginians had done, he was touched, and asked her what they stood in need of [...] Upon her making no reply, he sent for the officials appointed to attend on the women. When they presented themselves, and assured him that they kept the women generously supplied with all they required, she repeated her entreaty, upon which Scipio was still more puzzled, and conceiving the idea that the officials were neglecting their duty and had now made a false statement, he bade the women be of good cheer, saying that he would himself appoint other attendants, who would see to it that they were in want of nothing.

The old lady, after some hesitation, said, 'General, you do not take me rightly if you think that our present petition is about our food.' Scipio then understood what she meant, and noticing the youth and beauty of the daughters of Andobales and the other princes, he was forced to tears, recognizing in how few words she had pointed out to him the danger to which they were exposed. So now he made it clear to her that he understood, and grasping her hand bade her and the rest be of good cheer, for he would look after them as if they were his own sisters and children, and would appoint trustworthy men to attend them. (Polybius)

Source:

Hart, B. H. Liddell. "The Storm of Cartagena." Scipio Africanus Greater Than Napoleon. New York: Da Capo, 2004. 39, 40. Print.

There is a really good thread over in /v/technology which addresses this question. You can find that thread >>here<<.

TL;DR; - most OSS stacks are complete and utter dogshit when it comes to parallelism and concurrency. Python and Ruby have no concept of threading, for instance. So they scale out by running multiple processes per machine (1 per core usually) and lots of cheap, commodity machines per application.

.NET, on the other hand, has the best built-in concurrency tools out of any general purpose programming runtime (source: I port concurrent programming frameworks from JVM to .NET / CLR for a living) - so it scales by maximizing the hardware that it's on using threads, kernel caching, and etc. .NET scales vertically - by running on better hardware, not more of it.
